metadata.title: Scholarly discovery ontology profile
metadata.status: Pilot draft for review; existing vocabulary terms only

purpose: Specify the information needed to discover scholarly resources across a federation of knowledge graphs.

included: Topics and keywords when required by a selected CQ
Dataset membership in a federated metadata discovery catalogue
excluded: Endpoint routing and federated query execution
Guarantees that a described dataset is downloadable

use_cases.title: Citation discovery
use_cases.description: A researcher supplies a publication PID and retrieves article identifiers in either citation direction.

use_cases.title: Author citation discovery
use_cases.description: A researcher identifies an author and retrieves identifiers of documents citing that author's works.

use_cases.title: Dataset discovery
use_cases.description: A researcher discovers datasets described in participating graphs, optionally filtered by topic and keywords.

data_exchange_specification.description: Identifier-based discovery requests and results. Fields describe exchanged information, not automatically ontology classes or properties.

fields.name: publication_pid
fields.description: Input publication PID; its identifier scheme must be known.

fields.name: author_pid
fields.description: Pilot author identifier; name disambiguation is not implemented.

fields.name: result_pid
fields.description: Identifier of a returned article, document or dataset.

fields.name: source_graph
fields.description: An identifier for a participating source used by the application. The discovery catalogue aggregates dataset metadata from these sources; this input field does not require a new ontology class.

functional_requirements.text: Represent directed citations between scholarly works. Incoming citations can be queried using the same relation in reverse.
Represent authors as identifiable people or organisations and connect authored creative works to them using schema:author. Authorship is a relationship, not a newly minted Author class.
Represent identifiers for resource kinds required by the selected CQs, including the identifiers required in the expected answers.
Required dataset discovery information for the filtered discovery CQ.

rows.meaning: Subject concept associated with the dataset

functional_requirements.text: Represent dataset discovery as dataset listings in a federated discovery catalogue using existing DCAT terms. This is a catalogue of metadata collected from participating graphs; do not assert that every RDF graph is a dcat:Catalog. Actual graph routing remains outside this ontology profile.

non_functional_requirements.text: Deliver one ontology file with existing vocabulary terms, labels and definitions. The default serialization is RDF/XML (.owl); Turtle is optional. Human review is required before adoption.

terminology.definition: Persistent identifier. The pilot uses string values; identifier schemes and normalization require agreement.
A dataset described in a participating graph; this does not assert that its files can be downloaded.
A kind of publication; distinguish articles from other works when selecting the results of CQ_001.

modelling_decisions.text: Pilot simplification: identifier values may be literal properties. Do not infer OWL keys, functional properties or cardinality from the word unique.
Citations are directed. Prefer cito:cites queried in either direction; preserve published inverse relations when provided by the catalogue. Do not assert citation symmetry or transitivity.
Keep topics as concepts and keywords as literals for this pilot.

Use the existing schema:ScholarlyArticle -> schema:Article -> schema:CreativeWork hierarchy. CreativeWork is broader than publication; scholarly/documentary result types must be selected in queries. Dataset discovery uses a metadata catalogue, not a local SourceGraph class.

open_questions.text: Which PID schemes and normalization rules will be accepted?
Must CQ_001 return citation direction alongside article identifiers?
Does keyword filtering require all keywords or any keyword, and how are topic labels matched?

reuse_context: Use approved existing vocabulary IRIs only. Prefer schema:ScholarlyArticle for scholarly articles, schema:author for authorship, CiTO for citations, DCAT for dataset discovery and SKOS for topics. Do not mint local classes or properties.
additional_context: Editable pilot requirements. Existing terms and the catalogue-based discovery view require domain review. Graph endpoints, federation execution, identifier normalization and data mappings are application responsibilities.
